title: What cold water does to you in 60 seconds 🥶
subject: water
description:
Have you ever jumped into water that took your breath away? 👇

Cold water shock can start below 15°C (59°F): skin cooling triggers a gasp and breathing you can't control. Hypothermia expert Gordon Giesbrecht of the University of Manitoba sums up survival as 1-10-1: about 1 minute of cold shock, 10 minutes of useful movement, and roughly 1 hour before hypothermia causes unconsciousness. General information only, not medical advice.

Sources: RNLI ("Cold water shock: a bolt from the blue", 2016), McGill Office for Science and Society ("Professor Popsicle's physiological proof"), University of Portsmouth Extreme Environments Laboratory (cold water immersion studies)

scenes.text: Your first breath in cold water can be water.
Below about 15°C, the chill on your skin forces a gasp, then fast breathing you can't stop.
In an RNLI test, Olympic sailor Shirley Robertson entered a 12°C tank. "I could not control my breathing," she said.
Gordon Giesbrecht, at the University of Manitoba, calls it 1-10-1.
One minute of shock, 10 minutes of useful movement, an hour before hypothermia knocks you out.
Most cold water deaths come in those first minutes, long before your core gets cold.
